title: Prepare the fabrics
actions: Record supplier, lot, fiber content and care instructions for every material.
Condition or prewash according to supplier instructions; let fabric relax flat before measuring.
Mark right/wrong sides. Orient greatest usable stretch around the wearer, including across the narrow back insert.
Compare recovery of single body fabric, doubled band fabric and the insert. Keep test offcuts.
checks: No distorted or damaged fabric enters cutting.
The insert stretches more than the body; doubled bands are checked separately.
mistake: Do not infer stretch from material names or pull the fabric while cutting.

title: Qualify each seam on coupons
actions: Thread using the machine manual; record needle system, size and thread in each position.
Sew body-plus-insert, folded-band-plus-body and pocket-on-body coupons using the same layers as the garment.
Start with the manufacturer knit setting. Change only one setting at a time until feeding is flat.
Extend through the intended assembly use, release, and inspect. Keep the approved coupon and settings record.
checks: No thread cracking, skipped stitches, needle cuts or persistent waves.
Retest after thread, needle, material or layer changes.
mistake: No universal tension number or stitch length can substitute for these coupons.

title: Cut and mark six textile pieces
actions: Use the matching full-scale pattern variant, never the screen diagram. Cut two identical open #3 strips; do not mix variants.
Transfer center-front, pouch-zone boundaries, band midpoints and back-insert section marks into allowances.
Keep both support cutouts on the diagram left when viewed from inside. Mirror vertically for the upper support.
Mark free insertion edges in removable chalk. Do not snip notches into the finished seam line.
checks: Six pieces counted; cut lines and finished lines remain distinguishable.
No added hardware or closed band loops.
mistake: A finished {band_h}-inch band needs a {band_cut_h}-inch cut strip before folding.

title: Finish the lower free edge
actions: Test the cutout curve on scrap before handling the actual support.
Overedge only the free upper edge, including the left flange cutout, with the soft qualified edge finish.
Guide the curve without stretching it. Keep the knife from changing the finished opening.
Secure the chain tail with a blunt needle through the stitching; keep a sample for comparison.
checks: Flange opening retains its shape without a tight corded edge.
Sides and bottom still retain their attachment allowances.
mistake: Do not finish the cutout with a nonstretch straight seam or sew the opening shut.

title: Finish the upper free edge
actions: Lay the upper support in interior orientation: cutout on its lower left.
Finish the lower insertion edge and cutout using the same approved soft overedge operation.
Control the curve and secure tails without trimming into the flange clearance.
Place both supports together and confirm their cutouts face one another.
checks: Both flange reliefs are on the same diagram side.
The opposed free edges stay flexible and accessible.
mistake: A 180-degree rotation moves the cutout to the wrong side; use a vertical reflection.

title: Position the interior supports
actions: Lay #1 wrong side up. Center the bag envelope in the {zone}-inch pouch zone.
Turn under the {sa}-inch attachment allowances on support sides and outer perimeter, keeping free edges unfolded.
Place lower and upper supports around the bag envelope; align opposed cutouts around the flange.
Clip and mark the attachment perimeter. Remove the bag before any needle enters the work.
checks: Support width is centered within the expansion zone.
The facing free edges, flange and outlet remain outside attachment lines.
mistake: Do not sew the supports to each other across the central insertion opening.

title: Baste and check support access
actions: Baste the turned attachment perimeters through the supports and body only.
Insert the horizontal reference bag or mock-up; check insertion, removal and outlet access.
Use the depth gauge progressively up to {depth} inch outward from the local body plane. Check retention without forcing.
Remove the reference before sewing. If clearance fails, record the change needed and revise the shared design first.
checks: No flange or outlet obstruction at the tested depth.
Record this as preliminary support fit, not final garment validation.
mistake: A flat bag fitting does not prove that a filled pouch will fit.

title: Attach the lower support
actions: Keep #1 open and flat, wrong side up; move the upper support clear.
Use the approved stretch zigzag along the turned side and bottom perimeter, about 1/8 inch inside the folded edge.
Begin and end at the free-edge junctions. Secure ends with the tested machine method without a bulky dense tack.
Remove basting and check that only the intended layers were caught.
checks: Free top edge and flange cutout remain unstitched to #1.
Stitching stays on the turned allowance and extends without cracking.
mistake: Sewing across the free edge blocks insertion and changes the pocket function.

title: Attach the upper support
actions: Move the lower support clear and retain the marked upper-support position.
Attach only the turned sides and upper outer perimeter using the same qualified stretch zigzag.
Secure start/stop points, remove basting and inspect the exterior for puckering.
Recheck insertion and clearance with both supports attached, then remove the reference bag.
checks: The lower edge stays open; left cutouts align.
Both supports retain the reference without a seam crossing the flange.
mistake: Do not accidentally stitch the lower support into the upper perimeter.

title: Hem and mark the back insert
actions: Turn the short top and bottom edges by {hem} inch; coverstitch using the qualified needle spacing and hem coupon.
Finish before the long side seams. Do not stretch the narrow insert through the foot.
Mark the finished side edge into top {band_h} / middle {base} / bottom {band_h}-inch sections.
Retain {sa}-inch side seam allowances; secure all coverstitch ends per machine manual.
checks: Finished insert height is {back_h} inches.
Marks align with the future body-to-band seam junctions.
mistake: Do not reduce the insert to body-only height: it must also bridge both bands.

title: Fold the two open edge bands
actions: Fold each strip lengthwise, wrong sides together, aligning its two long raw edges.
Mark midpoint and the boundaries of the centered {zone}-inch attachment zone at the seam line.
Keep both short ends open with their joining allowances intact. Do not join them into loops.
Check the two pieces against each other before attaching either.
checks: Both strips are identical, with {band_h}-inch finished projection after joining.
Folded outer edges are clean and raw attachment edges align.
mistake: The elastic insert supplies the remaining back width; the bands must not bypass it.

title: Baste the top band flat
actions: Place the folded top band on the body right side with raw edges aligned at the upper attachment seam.
Match the center and pouch-zone boundaries, then the straight side sections.
Distribute the computed {excess}-inch excess only within the shaped zone using fine removable basting.
Turn the band outward and inspect the expansion shape; do not trim away the extra material.
checks: No hard pleats or severe puckering; compare with the opposite band.
Stop and revise pattern or material if the excess cannot be distributed cleanly.
mistake: Do not stretch the entire band or body to hide a local seam-length mismatch.

title: Sew the top attachment
actions: Remove the reference bag. Return the band to the basted joining position.
Join with the qualified four-thread overlock at the {sa}-inch allowance, catching body and both band layers.
Feed the shaped zone carefully; remove clips before the foot and do not cut the seam line.
Turn the band outward, settle allowance toward the body and inspect before removing remaining basting.
checks: Band projects {band_h} inches from its seam to folded edge.
The body still has outward ease; both short ends remain open.
mistake: Do not catch an interior support or free pocket edge in the band seam.

title: Baste the bottom and check depth
actions: Repeat alignment for the bottom band, with the same centered easing zone and open ends.
Temporarily clip the full-height insert to both assembled ends at the finished side seams.
Place on the curved fixture and measure outward depth up to {depth} inch; also check the top band and supports.
Remove the mock-up and temporary insert clips before returning to the machine.
checks: Reference remains insertable, removable and retained; outlet accessible.
Record results. Do not permanently sew if any required clearance fails.
mistake: Do not interpret the {max_h}-inch flat body height as proven outward capacity.

title: Sew the bottom attachment
actions: After the basting checkpoint passes, join the bottom band using the same allowance and seam formation as the top.
Catch the body and both band layers without catching the interior supports.
Turn outward and settle the allowance toward the body without heat that damages elastane.
Lay the assembly flat and align both full-height end edges for the back-insert seams.
checks: Top and bottom use identical fabric, folds and finished height.
Each assembled end matches the insert section marks.
mistake: An unequal seam allowance makes the two bands finish at different heights.

title: Join the first full-height back seam
actions: Place one finished insert edge against one end of the body-and-bands assembly, right sides together.
Match the top edge, upper band seam, lower band seam and bottom edge.
Sew one continuous qualified overlock seam through top band, body and bottom band at {sa} inch.
Keep the insert relaxed; grade bulk only after confirming seam security on the coupon.
checks: Section joins match top {band_h}, middle {base}, bottom {band_h} inches.
No hard ridge or skipped stitch at the layer transitions.
mistake: Joining only the body leaves both edge bands disconnected from the insert.

title: Close the second back seam
actions: Bring the remaining assembly end to the opposite insert edge, right sides together.
Check that the body and both bands form one untwisted loop. Match all section marks.
Sew the second full-height seam, taking care not to catch the opposite side of the loop.
Turn right side out and confirm the insert is centered at the back across the full height.
checks: Nominal relaxed seam-line circumference is {circ} inches before fabric behavior is evaluated.
Both bands terminate at the elastic insert rather than closing separately.
mistake: Stop if a band is twisted; do not solve it by cutting or adding an unrecorded seam.

title: Secure and finish the seams
actions: Secure every overlock and coverstitch end using the approved machine method; trim only loose tails.
Inspect side joins and band junctions for needle damage, seam cuts and missed layers.
{allowance_lay} Hold allowances flat only after coupon approval.
Keep fold edges and the exterior clean; decoration is optional and must not limit stretch.
checks: No unsecured chains or rough knots on the skin-facing surface.
No dense tack or topstitch restricts the back insert.
mistake: Do not pull thread tails until stitches unravel; do not bury bulky knots at the flange.

title: Inspect access and expansion
actions: On the fixture, insert the reference and test intermediate depth before the {depth}-inch target.
Measure perpendicular to the local body plane at the fullest part, not from the outer band edge.
Check flange/outlet access, retention, recovery and smooth band placement at each stage.
Assess required slip-on extension on a suitable fixture; record the limiting material or seam.
checks: No broken stitches, blocked opening or loss of retention.
Any failed function returns the affected pattern and instructions to review.
mistake: Passing a fixture check is not a measured compression or clinical performance claim.

title: Record the prototype results
actions: Record fabric lots, machine settings, dimensions, tested extension and all depth-check observations.
Launder only by the selected materials care instructions; record actual cycle and drying method.
Remeasure after relaxation and repeat access, seam and recovery checks.
Attach dated results and photos to the revision. Leave unperformed checks as requires retest.
checks: Every claimed pass has a dated record and tested configuration.
Material or geometry changes invalidate the affected result.
mistake: Do not label an informal wash or stretch check as ISO-compliant testing.
